scope: Synthesis of existing verified outputs; no new model or score. Official F1 primary.

completed_task_identity_pair.B_answer_changes: Old prior corrects SLAKE:13840 T2 to T1; refreshed prior corrects SLAKE:12997 T1 to T2. Each arm changes exactly one answer and no others.
completed_task_identity_pair.D_answer_changes: Both overrides leave all 228 predictions and all three per-item scores unchanged.
completed_task_identity_pair.interpretation: Correcting task identity is not sufficient to repair the cross-domain target-task result under these tested frozen-checkpoint interventions; it helps one content answer in the same-domain branch. Not a universal exclusion of routing errors.

train_mean_fixed_reference_sensitivity.construction: Final-model gate means over each cell's 1280 TRAIN prompts, averaged across five equal-sized stages; no TEST labels or parameter updates; not an optimized best fixed policy.
train_mean_fixed_reference_sensitivity.interpretation: The smaller cross-domain dynamic gain holds against uniform mixing, but not against this existing TRAIN-mean fixed reference. Do not generalize it to all fixed policies or infer that cross-domain training improves routing. This is arithmetic on existing verified results, not new scoring.

feasible_gate_fact.interpretation: Unit one-hot expert intervention lies outside original nondegenerate-prior gate family. Best-of-eight is external counterfactual reference, not attainable router oracle. Bounds alone do not prove this restriction causes the B/D gap.
feasible_gate_fact.uniform_feasibility: To realize uniform w_i=1/8, g_i=1/4-p_i must be nonnegative. Observed stage1 p_max=0.452168 in D violates this, so at least one layer cannot realize uniform with the original prior.

limits: Single seed and one shared target task; 228 QA/161 images.
Only descriptive decomposition, not mediation percentages.
TEST-selected best global expert is not a deployable baseline.
Stage1 actual outputs differ despite same nominal training and initialization.
Image exposure differs and posterior alias normalization changes some mechanism estimates.
Cross-domain task-identity zero effect excludes output changes under tested overrides, not all counterfactual routing failures.
